title: What the Choice Buys: a Pocket

scenes.visual: Title card: What the Choice Buys: a Pocket.

scenes.tts: Each neuron ends up with one kind of receptor. Does that mean it responds to only one odour?
scenes.visual: A single neuron with one receptor type on its cilia, surrounded by many odour molecules. Question mark.
scenes.narration: Each neuron ends up with one kind of receptor. Does that mean it responds to only one odour?

scenes.tts: The choice gives the neuron one kind of receptor. That receptor's binding pocket sets which molecules it responds to.
scenes.visual: Zoom into one receptor; its binding pocket glows.
scenes.narration: The choice gives the neuron one kind of receptor. That receptor's binding pocket sets which molecules it responds to.

scenes.tts: But one pocket does not mean one odour.
scenes.visual: Two very different molecules approach the same pocket.
scenes.narration: But one pocket does not mean one odour.

scenes.tts: Del Marmol, Yedlin and Ruta solved structures of an insect receptor from the bristletail, called M H O R five.
scenes.caption: Del Mármol, Yedlin and Ruta solved structures of an insect receptor from the bristletail, called MhOR5.
scenes.visual: A cryo-EM map of a four-part receptor rotates. Label: MhOR5, del Mármol, Yedlin and Ruta, 2021.
scenes.narration: Del Mármol, Yedlin and Ruta solved structures of an insect receptor from the bristletail, called MhOR5.

scenes.tts: It is built of four identical subunits, and it is itself an odorant-gated ion channel.
scenes.visual: The four subunits highlighted in turn; a central pore opens.
scenes.narration: It is built of four identical subunits, and it is itself an odorant-gated ion channel.

scenes.tts: The plant compound eugenol and the repellent deet sat in the same pocket. They are chemically unrelated.
scenes.caption: The plant compound eugenol and the repellent DEET sat in the same pocket. They are chemically unrelated.
scenes.visual: Eugenol and DEET structures shown side by side, then each placed in the same pocket.
scenes.narration: The plant compound eugenol and the repellent DEET sat in the same pocket. They are chemically unrelated.

scenes.tts: This insect channel is a contrast, not a template. Mammals use G-protein-coupled receptors.
scenes.visual: The insect channel slides aside; a seven-helix receptor slides in.
scenes.narration: This insect channel is a contrast, not a template. Mammals use G-protein-coupled receptors.

scenes.tts: Billesbolle and colleagues solved the active human receptor O R fifty-one E two, bound to propionate.
scenes.caption: Billesbølle and colleagues solved the active human receptor OR51E2, bound to propionate.
scenes.visual: The OR51E2 structure, PDB 8F76, rotates to show propionate inside the seven helices. Label: Billesbølle and colleagues, 2023.
scenes.narration: Billesbølle and colleagues solved the active human receptor OR51E2, bound to propionate.

scenes.tts: It was a purified, engineered complex with a mini G protein.
scenes.visual: A small G protein shape bound beneath the receptor. Label: engineered complex.
scenes.narration: It was a purified, engineered complex with a mini G protein.

scenes.tts: Humans carry about four hundred odorant receptors of this type. Mice carry about a thousand.
scenes.visual: Two counters: human, about 400; mouse, about 1,000.
scenes.narration: Humans carry about four hundred odorant receptors of this type. Mice carry about a thousand.

scenes.tts: In a cyclic A M P assay, two pocket mutants gained responses to longer-chain fatty acids.
scenes.caption: In a cAMP assay, two pocket mutants gained responses to longer-chain fatty acids.
scenes.visual: Residues F155 and L158 highlighted in the pocket; longer fatty-acid chains now fit.
scenes.narration: In a cAMP assay, two pocket mutants gained responses to longer-chain fatty acids.

scenes.tts: So is the mutant simply a better receptor? Take the mutant F one fifty-five A, and give it propionate.
scenes.caption: So is the mutant simply a better receptor? Take the mutant F155A, and give it propionate.
scenes.visual: Two dose-response curves begin to draw: wild type and F155A.
scenes.narration: So is the mutant simply a better receptor? Take the mutant F155A, and give it propionate.

scenes.tts: The E C fifty is the dose giving half the maximum. At the wild-type E C fifty, what fraction does the mutant give?
scenes.visual: Label first: model, Hill slope 1, zero baseline, each normalized to its own maximum. A cursor stops at 0.824 mM, the wild-type EC50. The wild-type curve reads 0.50; the mutant reading is hidden.
scenes.narration: The EC50 is the dose giving half the maximum. At the wild-type EC50, what fraction does the mutant give?
scenes.caption: The EC50 is the dose giving half the maximum. At the wild-type EC50, what fraction does the mutant give?

scenes.tts: In this model, about six percent of its own maximum. Its E C fifty is about fifteen times higher.
scenes.caption: In this model, about 6 percent of its own maximum. Its EC50 is about 15 times higher.
scenes.visual: The mutant reading appears: 0.063 (model value). An arrow spans the two EC50 values: 0.824 mM and 12.3 mM, about 15-fold.
scenes.narration: In this model, about 6 percent of its own maximum. Its EC50 is about 15 times higher.

scenes.tts: So the mutant is not simply better. It lost potency for propionate and gained responses to longer chains. Its selectivity shifted.
scenes.visual: Label: selectivity shift. Propionate down, longer chains up.
scenes.narration: So the mutant is not simply better. It lost potency for propionate and gained responses to longer chains. Its selectivity shifted.

scenes.tts: The size of the shift is uncertain. A second table in the paper gives a smaller one.
scenes.visual: A second, closer pair of curves fades in. On screen: about 6.5-fold.
scenes.narration: The size of the shift is uncertain. A second table in the paper gives a smaller one.

scenes.tts: These are functional values from cultured cells. They are not binding constants.
scenes.visual: Caution label: functional EC50, cultured cells.
scenes.narration: These are functional values from cultured cells. They are not binding constants.

scenes.tts: And a flat response would not prove a ligand cannot bind. Coupling, trafficking or the assay could be failing instead.
scenes.visual: A flat curve with four possible causes listed: no binding, no coupling, no trafficking, assay ceiling.
scenes.narration: And a flat response would not prove a ligand cannot bind. Coupling, trafficking or the assay could be failing instead.

scenes.tts: Now look back at the three phases. Silence every gene. Let a few compete. Lock in the winner.
scenes.visual: The three phase panels from chapter 1 return: silenced, competing, locked in.
scenes.narration: Now look back at the three phases. Silence every gene. Let a few compete. Lock in the winner.

scenes.tts: The lock holds one receptor in place. That receptor's pocket decides which molecules the neuron responds to.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: one gene chosen and locked; its pocket sets what the neuron responds to.
scenes.narration: The lock holds one receptor in place. That receptor's pocket decides which molecules the neuron responds to.

scenes.visual: End card: What the Choice Buys: a Pocket.
